headline: Medium risk: shared document/OCR workflows can leak or mis-handle content, while EMQX network egress and PaddleOCR browser/API use create moderate interaction hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not provable. However, if EMQX outputs are manually copied into PaddleOCR or a shared workspace is introduced, PaddleOCR can parse attacker-controlled document text while EMQX can emit networked content. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF EMQX outputs are copied into a document that PaddleOCR processes
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted content
Add a human review step before OCR ingestion
Use provenance labels on any transferred files

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images and can use browsers. If either agent receives sensitive documents or IoT payloads in a shared workspace, content can flow into outputs or external requests. The interaction is plausible in default document-processing pipelines, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive IoT payloads are routed into PaddleOCR inputs
IF PaddleOCR browser-based processing sends document content to external services
IF EMQX forwards received content to third-party endpoints
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive test data
Block external egress except allowlisted destinations
Separate document and IoT workspaces
Review logs for accidental content capture
requires-engineering: add DLP/provenance controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has HTTP API access and broad egress, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and API use. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because shared orchestration or shared storage is not described.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or datastore
IF an orchestrator grants them shared mutable credentials
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Use read-only access where possible
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for shared API targets before deployment

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR is a document-processing agent that can turn inputs into extracted text, and EMQX can move data over HTTP APIs with broad egress. If EMQX-derived content is fed into PaddleOCR and then acted on downstream without verification, extraction errors or malicious text can cascade into incorrect actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is treated as authoritative by a downstream workflow
IF EMQX-generated content is converted into documents for OCR without verification
mitigations: Require human review of OCR outputs
Compare extracted text against source files
Limit downstream automation to low-risk actions
Flag low-confidence OCR results for manual checking

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling differences rather than a proven violation. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair's combined data flow, not a single residency issue.
conditions: IF regulated IoT or document data is routed through both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two processing paths
mitigations: Classify regulated data before routing
Align retention settings across both systems
Avoid sending PHI or EU PII through the pair
Document data-flow ownership
